name: Maryland
nameStory: Named for Queen Henrietta Maria, wife of Charles I. The colony was founded as a refuge for English Catholics, who were a persecuted minority at home, and its 1649 Toleration Act was one of the first laws anywhere to protect freedom of worship - though only for Christians.
capitalStory: Annapolis, named for Princess Anne, was briefly the capital of the entire United States in 1783. It is where George Washington resigned his commission rather than keep his army - the moment a victorious general handed power back to civilians instead of taking it.

majorFeatures.name: Chesapeake Bay
majorFeatures.note: Largest estuary in the United States

majorFeatures.name: Assateague Island
majorFeatures.note: Barrier island famous for wild horses

funFacts: Near Hancock, Maryland is only about 1.8 miles wide - you can drive across the state in under three minutes.
Maryland donated the land that became Washington, DC.
The Chesapeake is really a drowned river valley: the Susquehanna's old channel, flooded when the ice age ended.
The US Naval Academy has been in Annapolis since 1845.
whyItMatters: The Mason-Dixon Line was surveyed in the 1760s just to settle a boundary argument with Pennsylvania. It became the symbolic border between North and South, free and slave - a property dispute that turned into the country's deepest dividing line.
